card.name: Words just before a sentence's main point
card.fires_on: Scattered ordinary words in general web prose, often a pronoun, conjunction or verb that sits right before the main clause or key point is delivered. No single word type dominates.

modes.label: Clause-opening words
modes.description: A short linking or subject word such as 'that', 'it', 'when' or 'answer' just before the main statement.
modes.example: Finally,<< it>> hit him: Give them harder material.

modes.label: Partway through a verb
modes.description: The start of a verb split into pieces, such as 'capt' in 'captivated' or 'ex' in 'exclaims'.
modes.example: “Nobody was killed, thank goodness,”<< ex>>claims Blake, “But it does raise

modes.label: Word before a result phrase
modes.description: A word like 'all', 'as' or 'may' that precedes the continuation of advice or an explanation.
modes.example: If you notice your baby isn't moving<< as>> much, call your doctor.
